lesson.summary: Understand the jack of all trades from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Object Tools & Design

stage.description: Namespaces, attributes, closures, generators, reflection, plus OOP design principles such as SOLID.

payload.code:
Is your class trying to do too many things at once? If so, see if you can list the
responsibilities of the class. You may find that one of them will form the basis of a good
class itself.
    Leaving an overzealous class unchanged can cause particular problems if you create
subclasses. Which responsibility are you extending with the subclass? What would you
do if you needed a subclass for more than one responsibility? You are likely to end up
with too many subclasses or an overreliance on conditional code.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
UML Class & Sequence: Standard diagrams for static structure and runtime interaction.
Unit of Work: Tracking changes to many objects and writing them in a single transaction.
